subproblem.title: Density gap for minimizing cones
subproblem.statement: For all P, j ∈ ℕ with j ≥ 1 there is δ > 0 with the following property: if C ∈ 𝒟_j(ℝ^P) is minimizing in ℝ^P (IsMinimizingIn C univ), ∂C = 0, C is a cone (IsConeCurrent C) and HasMassDensity C 0 θ (Θ^j(μ_C, 0) = θ) with θ < 1 + δ, then θ ≤ 1.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) j) (θ : ℝ), IsMinimizingIn C univ → BoundaryVanishes C → IsConeCurrent C → HasMassDensity C 0 θ → θ < 1 + δ → θ ≤ 1
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent gap lemma G, part (c) (which is all that the frozen statement needs; parts (a) and (b) of G are not used), with the siblings compactness_of_minimizing_currents and density_one_implies_regular in place of Allard's theorem along sequences (departure [D3] of the parent). μ_A denotes the measure of any representation of an integer multiplicity A (sibling child im_mass_measure: all representations have the same measure (c), M_W(A) = μ_A(W) for open W (a), spt A = spt μ_A (b)); ω_j := unitBallVolume j.
0. If j > P, every j-covector on ℝ^P is zero, so every C ∈ 𝒟_j(ℝ^P) is 0 and its density at 0 is θ = 0 ≤ 1; δ := 1 works. Assume j ≤ P and, for a contradiction, that no δ > 0 works. Then for every i ≥ 1 there is a cone C_i as in the statement with θ_i := Θ^j(μ_{C_i}, 0) ∈ (1, 1 + 1/i).
1. (Cone masses.) For a cone C, η_{0,λ#}C = C and M_W(η_{0,λ#}C) = λ^{−j}M_{λW}(C) give μ_C(λA) = λ^jμ_C(A) for Borel A and λ > 0; hence μ_C(B_ρ(0)) = ρ^jμ_C(B_1(0)) for all ρ > 0, Θ^j(μ_C, 0) = μ_C(B_1(0))/ω_j, μ_C({0}) = 0, and μ_C(∂B_ρ(0)) = 0 for every ρ > 0 (by homogeneity μ_C(∂B_ρ(0)) = ρ^jμ_C(∂B_1(0)); if μ_C(∂B_1(0)) > 0, the uncountably many disjoint spheres ∂B_ρ(0), 1 < ρ < 2, would each have measure ≥ μ_C(∂B_1(0)) > 0 inside B_2(0), which has finite measure). In particular μ_{C_i}(B_R(0)) = ω_jR^jθ_i ≤ 2ω_jR^j for all R > 0 and i.
2. (Limit cone.) By the weak compactness lemma (Simon Ch. 6, 2.15) applied on the balls B_R(0), R ∈ ℕ, with a diagonal argument, a subsequence (not relabelled) satisfies C_i ⇀ C in 𝒟_j(ℝ^P) (WeaklyConvergesOn on U = ℝ^P). The sibling compactness_of_minimizing_currents (DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1, frozen type CompactnessOfMinimizingCurrents), applied with U = ℝ^P (after transporting along Euclid P = Euclid (j + (P − j))): its mass hypothesis holds because sup_i(M_W(C_i) + boundaryMassOn C_i W) ≤ 2ω_jR^j < ∞ for W ⊆ B_R(0) (∂C_i = 0); hence C is integer multiplicity and minimizing in ℝ^P, and μ_{C_i} → μ_C (MassMeasuresConverge). Moreover ∂C = 0 (C(dω) = lim C_i(dω) = 0) and C is a cone (C(η_{0,λ}^#ω) = lim C_i(η_{0,λ}^#ω) = lim C_i(ω) = C(ω)).
3. (Density one.) By step 1 for C, μ_C(∂B_1(0)) = 0, so the convergence of mass measures gives μ_{C_i}(B_1(0)) → μ_C(B_1(0)) (approximate 1_{B_1(0)} from above and below by continuous compactly supported functions). Hence Θ^j(μ_C, 0) = μ_C(B_1(0))/ω_j = lim θ_i = 1, i.e. HasMassDensity C 0 1 (by step 1 the ratio μ_C(B_ρ(0))/(ω_jρ^j) is constant in ρ).
4. (Regularity of the approximating cones.) Apply the sibling density_one_implies_regular (DAG node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1, frozen type DensityOneImpliesRegular) with U = N = ℝ^P (ℓ = k := P − j, after transporting along Euclid P = Euclid (j + k); ℝ^P is an embedded C² P-dimensional submanifold with closure ℝ^P ∖ ℝ^P = ∅), Ts := (C_i), T := C, ys :≡ 0, y := 0. Its hypotheses hold: each C_i and C are minimizing in ℝ^P ∩ ℝ^P with supports in ℝ^P and BoundaryVanishes; sup_i M_W(C_i) ≤ 2ω_jR^j < ∞ for W ⊆ B_R(0); C_i ⇀ C; 0 ∈ ℝ^P; HasMassDensity C 0 1 (step 3); and 0 ∈ spt C_i, because otherwise μ_{C_i}(B_ε(0)) = 0 for some ε > 0 and θ_i = 0. Hence 0 ∈ reg C_i (regularSet C_i) for all large i.
5. (Contradiction.) For such i, the sibling child regular_point_density gives m_i ∈ ℕ with HasMassDensity C_i 0 m_i; by uniqueness of the density, θ_i = m_i ∈ ℕ. But θ_i ∈ (1, 1 + 1/i) ⊆ (1, 2) contains no integer. Hence some δ > 0 has the required property.
proof_key_steps: Argue by contradiction with minimizing cones C_i whose vertex densities θ_i lie in (1, 1 + 1/i); cones have μ(B_R) = ω_jR^jθ_i ≤ 2ω_jR^j.
Weak compactness and the sibling compactness_of_minimizing_currents give a minimizing limit cone C with μ_{C_i} → μ_C.
μ_C(∂B_1) = 0 for cones, so Θ(C, 0) = lim θ_i = 1.
The sibling density_one_implies_regular (with y_i = 0 ∈ spt C_i) gives 0 ∈ reg C_i for large i, and regular_point_density makes θ_i an integer in (1, 2): contradiction.

audit.reason: The contradiction argument verifies compactness and density-one regularity hypotheses, then contradicts integer densities at regular points. It proves the exact weaker conclusion θ ≤ 1 and handles j > P separately.
